problem: Portable human demonstrations need robot-compatible motion, timing and visual observations before they can train deployable manipulation policies.
contribution: UMI combines a handheld gripper, matched wrist-camera views, visual-inertial motion recovery, relative action trajectories and measured latency alignment.
algorithm: Collect gripper trajectories and width, filter for target kinematic feasibility, train a diffusion policy on synchronized observations, and execute only future-valid action samples after compensating observation, inference and actuator delay.
observations: Matched fisheye wrist RGB, relative end-effector history and gripper width; bimanual policies additionally use relative inter-gripper pose in a shared map.
actions: A timed sequence of end-effector poses relative to the current pose at each policy query, plus continuous gripper width. This differs from per-step delta integration and global absolute coordinates.
embodiment_and_data: Portable handheld grippers deployed on multiple arms; real cup arrangement, dynamic tossing, bimanual cloth folding and long-horizon dish washing.
experiments: Matched-initialization task tests, latency/representation ablations, cross-embodiment and environment generalization, collection throughput and motion-capture tracking accuracy.
baselines: Alternative camera/action/latency representations, teleoperation collection and policy ablations; compare task outcomes rather than assuming a handheld interface is equivalent to bare-hand video.

quantitative_result.predicate: Cup upright on saucer, handle within15degrees of target direction
quantitative_result.scope: Narrow specified task setup, not universal transfer.

limitations: Kinematic infeasibility is filtered rather than solved universally. VisualSLAM requires texture; target gripper/camera geometry must match the demonstration interface. An overhead-only camera does not inherit UMI's matched-wrist observation assumptions.
hardware_adaptation: Adapt relative trajectories, capture-time interpolation and stale-action rejection, but measure actual Pi/NX/Nano latency. Keep explicit hand-eye/object registration for Explorer's different grippers and camera placement.
algorithm_detail: Each action chunk uses one current gripper frame, avoiding accumulated deltas. Observation streams are aligned to the delayed camera timestamp; actions already obsolete after total pipeline delay are discarded. Bimanual relative pose comes from a common scene map, not an uncalibrated pair of camera images.
integration_contract: Store per-stream capture timestamps, clock domain/uncertainty, measured input/execution delays, pose frame, metric units, gripper calibration and feasible workspace. Recheck these bindings after changing a camera or robot profile.
license_evidence: Official repository metadata identifies MIT at the pinned commit. No model/dataset license or source-code execution was audited, so timing concepts are adapted without claiming upstream hardware parity.
required_experiments: Measure p50/p95/p99 observation-to-dispatch and execution delay under camera load; reject expired chunks; pose/width round-trip and workspace tests; matched source/target scene evaluation; supervised physical validation after approval.
difference_from_explorer: UMI already provides transferable relative action interfaces and latency matching. Explorer must test additional skill memory, cross-gripper effects and independent outcome/retention mechanisms.
